Strait of Hormuz Status: October 11, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  224 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
11 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.72 + 0.42 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain reports US forces struck a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman as two more tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

02 Al Jazeera reports IRGC warned against ignoring the waterway's security rules as CENTCOM said it disabled a vessel attempting to run the blockade.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, and attacks on merchant shipping are continuing at an accelerated pace. gCaptain reports that two more tankers were struck in the strait and that US forces disabled a cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman that CENTCOM says was attempting to run the blockade. Al Jazeera reports the IRGC warned against ignoring the waterway's security rules as US-Iran tensions show no sign of easing. gCaptain and blue News separately report another tanker hit in the strait; gCaptain and multiple regional outlets also report a tanker caught fire after a projectile strike. The attacker has not been identified by any maritime authority. UK Maritime Trade Operations confirms a tanker was damaged by an unidentified projectile, per reporting carried by Türkiye Today and The Times of Israel. Iran's IRGC claims a supertanker exploded after striking a mine in the strait; no maritime authority has confirmed that account and US Central Command disputes Iranian claims about the waterway's status. On the diplomatic track, Iran has said it will respond to Washington's reply to its seven-day plan within days, but no terms have been published and parliament speaker Ghalibaf has said the strait will not reopen until Iran's seven conditions are met. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent settled at $104.72 at Friday's close, up 0.42% on the session; futures are shut. As of 15:20 UTC, 130 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
